maintenance.action: Replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0050-002

Asset: WELL-0050 (SW-23 Well 050, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 13 Jan 2023 08:00 · Finished: 25 Jan 2023 22:00 · Well stopped for this job: 302 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Daniel Foster Triggered by: inspection INS-0050-0012 on 2023-01-12 Report written: 25 Jan 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0050-0012 showed the wellhead at 7.6 °C with the air at 8.2 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 11 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Winding breakdown from heat and age.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 1 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

V-belts956

Labour (company crew)5,764

Notes and recommendations

  • Clean the motor cooling fins at each scheduled service.
  • Summer heat raises the risk of motor trips on this field.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0050-012

Asset: WELL-0050 (SW-23 Well 050, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 17 Aug 2024 08:00 · Finished: 21 Aug 2024 21:00 · Well stopped for this job: 109 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0050-0094 on 2024-08-15 Report written: 27 Aug 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0050-0094 showed the wellhead at 37.3 °C with the air at 33.5 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 3 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 8 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Saddle bearing assembly1,986
Bolts, shims and seals496
Bearing grease and consumables828
Labour (company crew)2,664
Total5,974

Notes and recommendations

  • Shorten the grease interval on this unit to 60 days.
  • Check saddle bearings on neighbouring units of the same age.
  • HSE to follow up on the WS-07 item above with the crew.

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0050-021

Asset: WELL-0050 (SW-23 Well 050, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 13 Mar 2026 08:00 · Finished: 14 Mar 2026 05:00 · Well stopped for this job: 21 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0050-0175 on 2026-03-12 Report written: 14 Mar 2026

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0050-0175 at 12:30 on 2026-03-12 found crude oil on the pad: about 3.6% of the pad area, estimated 0.8 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 8.5 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 245 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 196 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 1.3 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0050-021 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.38% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).
